title: Do leafcutter ants eat leaves?
hook: They carry leaves all day long, but they don’t eat them.
summary: No: leafcutter ants use the leaves to grow a fungus, and the fungus is what they eat.

cardBlocks.text: Watching a line of ants carrying leaf pieces, you might think they plan to eat them. They don’t. Leafcutter ants take the leaves into the nest and use them to feed a fungus they grow there, like a garden. They do drink a little sap, but their food is the fungus.

The fungus breaks down plant material that the ants’ digestive enzymes can’t, making it usable as food. It is the colony’s only food source: if the fungus dies, the colony dies too. Ants started farming fungus about 50 million years ago, long before humans.
Leafcutter ants don’t eat leaves: they use leaves to grow a fungus, and they eat the fungus.

deepDiveBlocks.text: When a young queen leaves to found a new colony, she carries a piece of fungus in her mouth. For the first month she stays underground tending the garden while she waits for her workers to grow up.

This partnership between ants and fungus is thought to have started in the Amazon basin. Since then it has spread to more than 250 ant species in the Americas. The farmed fungus exists only alongside the ants.
